attempts.summary: Implemented node2↔node3 traffic shaping through VyOS router node1 via an Ansible playbook run from control node4. node2 (lan-a, 10.10.10.0/24) and node3 (lan-b, 10.10.20.0/24) got static IPs on their second NIC via nmcli plus routes to each other's subnet via node1. node1 got static addresses on eth1/eth2 and a VyOS qos shaper policy (HTB, 1mbit) applied as an egress policy on eth2 (facing node3), capping all node2→node3 traffic to 1 Mbit/s while eth1 (facing node2) stays unshaped for the reverse direction. Verified with iperf3: node2→node3 settled at ~1.04 Mbit/s, node3→node2 reached ~1.5+ Gbit/s unrestricted. All four nodes were restarted one at a time with boot_id changes proving real reboots, and all state (static IPs, routes, VyOS shaper config) was confirmed to persist. Caught and fixed a reconciler gotcha: an ad-hoc SSH key drop into VyOS's authorized_keys file was wiped on reboot by VyOS's login reconciler; replaced with a proper `set system login user vyos authentication public-keys` config entry which persisted, and re-ran the playbook to confirm idempotency and full recovery.
